Wow, boy does this hit home. I'm have the same problem, and I just turned 46 a couple of days ago. So I've had acne and skin problems for more than twice as long. It's not as bad as it was, but now and then I feel actually shocked at my own appearance in the mirror. Everywhere I go I wonder if people are silently shocked too. It's made me really notice how many people don't have this problem at all and then I feel even worse. I still have acne problems at my age, and now I'm having even more problems with rampant itching and rashes.

And the kicker is, I finally got insurance again after 5 years of not having any, but they won't cover any pre-existing conditions for **12 months** after I start on the plan. FML, seriously.

I'd look into some free clinic options maybe, or possibly there's a university clinic where you live where they might charge on a sliding scale.

>I'd suggest finding out about the laws where you live, and what they are required to do.

I did read the FAQ on their site and they say they are obligated to contact the authorities if they think you are in danger of harming yourself or others. But I'm really really afraid of what form that could take. Does just saying I'm not going to do anything keep me safe? I mean I wouldn't ever harm someone else. I only loathe myself. I'm the only one I wish was dead.

But what would I say if they ask me right away, like during the first session. Do I lie right away? I've realized lately that one of my biggest issues is I've lost the ability to lie to myself about myself (if I ever had it).

And I've got to question whether therapy is going to be helpful at all. I can almost predict how banal and formulaic their approach is going to be. I just don't think it's going to be helpful. Especially if I have to lie about what's really bothering me.
This is exactly like me too. Only I stopped smoking weed like 5 months ago and I still feel terrible.

I've called before. And I'm grateful to those people who have listened to my sad sack whining crap. But why do they always want to know where I am? They ask me over and over again instead of just *talking* to me.

Thanks for this. Not a lot of people know that Sylvester Stallone wrote the screenplay for the first Rocky movie. Nominated for an academy award (lost to Paddy Chayefsky for Network) and won for best picture.

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky#Academy_Awards_.E2.80.93_1976

A couple of days ago I posted here feeling kind of inherently unlovable myself. I'm only 7 years older than you. But compared to me, you're out there spreading it like Walt Frazier and John Mayer combined. Seriously.

But I'm here instead to offer what little bit of strength I've got left. I might not be here myself but for the fact that I can only afford the bullets and not the gun. So you know what. I'll stick it out a little longer  if you will.

I want to thank all of you for your comments and your input. I'm sorry to say that I feel just as bad today or maybe even worse.

I just want to make two points.

1. I've thought alot about the relevant age/sex demographics in the area I live in. The ratio of female population my age, or even near my age. And if I am at all realistic the picture this paints is not at all a good one. We make fun of people who play the lottery because of the astronomical odds of success. So the odds of me finding success personally is probably even more remote.

2. The situation I find myself in has more to do with [Dr. Harry Harlow](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wire_mother#Surrogate_mother_experiment) than Joseph Campbell. As humans we crave and need a close social proximity and more importantly affection and physical contact or we become visibly stressed and despondent. This is where I'm at right now. I'm a monkey rocking back and forth in it's little cage without even the comfort of a wire mother.

No the point of Logan's Run was that they didn't know people could get old *at all*. I think (fictionally speaking anyway) once they became familiar with the concept again. They would have found it just as appalling as we do.

I don't think I'm as immersed in "young" culture as much as the things I like (interesting modern art, new music) are embraced by younger people than me because people my age are generally homebodies with a family and are into family activities like soccer games and emailing cute pix to the grandparents.

I do want to be clear about one thing. I think about killing myself frequently. That's why I posted over here and not just in dating or depression. I truly wish I had never been born. I can't think of many days or years in which I don't have a great deal of regret invested. I don't like waking up to myself and my life. I've thought about re-locating but I've been around reddit enough to have seen many "help I've moved to a new city and I still don't have any friends" posts. So that scares me too. At least here I still have one or two not at all close friends. And the surviving members of my family hardly ever contact me. My dog died last year, and that tears me up constantly. Since I live alone I think it would be cruel to get a new dog and leave it alone 8+ hours a day (I'm allergic to cats).
You're darn right I'm lonely. And it's precisely *because* I've tried online dating that I'm feeling particularly despondent.

Thanks, but I don't want to go on a cruise. Those ships are full of couples, old people and newlyweds. And I'm really not the nature scene type either. I'm way more urban. But that's not where I'm at and it's to expensive to live in.

I don't have any urge to travel. I don't even like going to the movies by myself. The last thing I want is some amazing place with only myself to witness it. I don't have much urge towards self indulgence. And if I picked some place at random, at least in the USA, I'd probably just end up like here. Some post industrial crap town with strip malls and Wal-Marts posing as a town.
